questions.text: Is a child or teenager a central character?
questions.definition: A principal viewpoint or focal character is under 20 during the main story; childhood flashbacks alone do not count.

questions.text: Is a woman or girl a central character?
questions.definition: At least one principal viewpoint or focal character is female. This is not the complement of q03.

questions.text: Is a man or boy a central character?
questions.definition: At least one principal viewpoint or focal character is male. This is not the complement of q02.

questions.text: Does the story follow several equally important characters?
questions.definition: The narrative has multiple principal characters rather than one dominant protagonist.

questions.text: Is a nonhuman character central to the story?
questions.definition: A principal focal character is an animal, artificial intelligence, or other nonhuman being; an incidental creature does not count.

questions.text: Is a student a central character?
questions.definition: A principal focal character attends a school or university during the main story.

questions.text: Is a detective or investigator a central character?
questions.definition: A principal focal character performs sustained crime investigation; an incidental mystery does not count.

questions.text: Does a central character have supernatural abilities openly established in the premise?
questions.definition: Abilities must be established in the premise, not revealed in a later twist.

questions.text: Is a school a major setting?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the main story takes place at a school or university.

questions.text: Does much of it take place in a large city?
questions.definition: An urban setting dominates a substantial part of the main narrative.

questions.text: Does much of it take place in a village or rural area?
questions.definition: A village, farm, or countryside dominates a substantial part of the main narrative.

questions.text: Does much of it take place in Korea?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the story is geographically set on the Korean peninsula; author nationality is irrelevant.

questions.text: Does much of it take place in Britain?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the story is set in Great Britain; author nationality is irrelevant.

questions.text: Does much of it take place in the United States?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the story is set in the USA; author nationality is irrelevant.

questions.text: Is it mainly set in an invented world?
questions.definition: An invented secondary world, rather than recognizable real-world Earth, is the primary setting.

questions.text: Does a major part take place aboard a ship or at sea?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the narrative takes place at sea or aboard a waterborne ship.

questions.text: Is most of the story set before 1900?
questions.definition: More than half of the main narrative is set before 1900. Publication year is not setting year.

questions.text: Is most of it set between 1900 and 1945?
questions.definition: More than half of the main narrative is set in 1900 through 1945 inclusive.

questions.text: Is most of it set between 1946 and 1999?
questions.definition: More than half of the main narrative is set in 1946 through 1999 inclusive.

questions.text: Is most of it set in the 2000s or later, excluding an imagined future?
questions.definition: Most of the main narrative is set in real-world 2000 or later and is not speculative future fiction.

questions.text: Is it set in an imagined future?
questions.definition: A speculative future society or future era is the primary setting, relative to the work when written.

questions.text: Does it take place across multiple historical periods?
questions.definition: Substantial narrative spans distinctly different historical periods, not merely a brief flashback.

questions.text: Has a large disaster already changed society when the story begins?
questions.definition: The main story starts after a society-altering disaster; a disaster late in the story does not count.

questions.text: Is a real historical war a major part of the setting?
questions.definition: An identifiable real historical war substantially shapes the main setting.

questions.text: Is solving a crime a main storyline?
questions.definition: Crime investigation is a central ongoing plot, rather than an incidental event.

questions.text: Is a romantic relationship a main storyline?
questions.definition: Developing or sustaining a romantic relationship is a central plot.

questions.text: Is a long journey a main storyline?
questions.definition: A sustained journey or quest drives a substantial part of the plot.

questions.text: Is surviving physical danger a main storyline?
questions.definition: Survival under ongoing physical threat is a central plot.

questions.text: Is conflict within a family a main storyline?
questions.definition: Relationships or conflict among family members drive a main plot.

questions.text: Is resisting a government or authority a main storyline?
questions.definition: Opposition to a governing or institutional power is central to the premise.

questions.text: Is a competition or tournament central to the premise?
questions.definition: An organized contest, tournament, or competitive selection is central to the advertised premise.

questions.text: Does the story prominently involve magic?
questions.definition: Overt magic materially shapes the main narrative; a metaphor alone does not count.

questions.text: Is time travel part of the premise?
questions.definition: Literal movement through time is established in the premise; ordinary flashbacks do not count.

questions.text: Is space travel part of the premise?
questions.definition: Travel beyond Earth is established in the premise.

questions.text: Are ghosts or spirits openly part of the premise?
questions.definition: Ghosts or spirits are openly established, rather than a concealed ending or figurative reference.

questions.text: Are animals that speak or behave like people prominent?
questions.definition: Anthropomorphized animals are prominent characters, not a single incidental pet.

questions.text: Is a prison or confinement a major setting?
questions.definition: Prison, detention, captivity, or comparable forced confinement is a substantial setting.

questions.text: Is a shop or workplace a major setting?
questions.definition: A shop, office, factory, or comparable workplace is a substantial setting.

questions.text: Is illness a major part of the premise?
questions.definition: An illness or epidemic is openly central to the premise.

questions.text: Does the story prominently involve moving to another country?
questions.definition: Immigration, exile, or relocation across countries is substantial; tourism alone is insufficient.

questions.text: Is the story intended to be frightening?
questions.definition: Horror, sustained fear, or deliberate frightening effects are prominent; subjective label, use conservative confidence.

questions.text: Is humor a major part of it?
questions.definition: Comedy or satire is a sustained defining effect, rather than occasional jokes.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on growing up?
questions.definition: Maturation or coming of age is a major theme.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on social class or inequality?
questions.definition: Class, wealth disparity, or social inequality is a major theme.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on friendship?
questions.definition: Friendship is a major thematic focus, not merely the presence of friends.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on loneliness or isolation?
questions.definition: Loneliness or social isolation is a major thematic focus.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on grief or loss?
questions.definition: Grieving or loss is a major thematic focus; do not expose a death revealed only in a twist.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on moral or philosophical questions?
questions.definition: Explicit ethical or philosophical inquiry is a sustained major theme.

questions.text: Is much of it narrated using “I”?
questions.definition: First-person narration constitutes a substantial part of the novel; a quote in a synopsis is not evidence.

questions.text: Does it switch between different characters’ viewpoints?
questions.definition: The novel uses multiple focal viewpoints; a synopsis describing several characters does not prove this.

questions.text: Is much of it presented as letters or diary entries?
questions.definition: Epistolary or diary form constitutes a substantial part of the work.

questions.text: Does it frequently move between past and present?
questions.definition: Repeated nonlinear switching between time periods is a defining structural feature.

questions.text: Is it part of a named series?
questions.definition: This individual work belongs to an explicitly named series; a film franchise alone is insufficient.

questions.text: Is it the first book in that series?
questions.definition: The source establishes it as volume one in a named series; do not infer from a familiar title.

questions.text: Does it follow a family across more than one generation?
questions.definition: The main story substantially follows successive generations of one family.

questions.text: Is it a short novel or novella rather than a long novel?
questions.definition: Use Yes only if a source explicitly classifies the work as a novella or short novel. Edition page counts alone are insufficient.
questions.inactive_reason: Define 'short novel' consistently before enabling; edition page counts are unreliable.

questions.text: Was it originally written in Korean?
questions.definition: Original composition language, not the language of this edition or author nationality.

questions.text: Was it originally written in English?
questions.definition: Original composition language, not the language of this edition or author nationality.

questions.text: Was it originally written in Japanese?
questions.definition: Original composition language, not the language of this edition or author nationality.

questions.text: Was it first published before 1900?
questions.definition: First publication of the work, not a translation, reissue, or edition. An unverified source date is insufficient.

questions.text: Was it first published in 2000 or later?
questions.definition: First publication of the work, not a translation, reissue, or edition.

questions.text: Has it been adapted into a feature film?
questions.definition: A released feature-film adaptation of this work, not another volume. Absence from a 2012 synopsis does not establish No.

questions.text: Has it been adapted into a television or streaming series?
questions.definition: A released television or streaming adaptation of this work. Future announcements alone do not count.

questions.text: Was its author awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature?
questions.definition: Award received by the author by 2026-11-14. Old snapshots cannot establish a current No.
